steps.what: Read the teacher's actual game instructions and current pupil participation requirements
Organize the actual games, physical space and recreational materials for the participating pupils
Supervise games and recreational activities, supporting physical, mental and social development through actual participation

tasks.design: Link existing activity instructions in {DOCS}; keep physical organization and supervision with the assistant using recreational equipment {OTHER}. Only repeated reference navigation changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual game instructions can require separate document openings.
tasks.enabler_now: A native activity link can remove those openings.
tasks.still_hard: Participation, inclusion and changing physical activity require live supervision.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant responds to children and supports safe, inclusive participation.

ambition.what: The same recreational activity stays supervised by a person.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing activity links can reduce navigation but do not replace physical recreation supervision.

assumptions: Boundary is actual instruction reading, physical organization and live supervision. Do not invent a post-game report or a participation log. {OTHER} means physical recreational equipment.

The responsible teacher supplies the existing activity goal, instructions and participation requirements; s1 counts reading and manual fallback, s2 all setup and s3 all supervision. No new data capture is assumed. Test native links first; remove only 1 of 5 navigation units and retain 4 reading units, with all physical work retained.
These are unmeasured task estimates. No model, recording, pupil scoring or send is proposed. Link repair beyond normal reading is additional upkeep below.
research_questions: Observe actual instruction lookup, setup and supervision separately.

already_counted.description: Reading, setup and complete supervision remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: Maintain and repair the activity reference links beyond normal reading.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=4+20+75=99. Gross1 less0.5 upkeep gives0.5. Conservative case: an unfamiliar game retains4.5 of5 lookup units; its0.5 gain just covers upkeep. Physical work stays unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read the actual staff-meeting agenda and relevant committee papers
Attend staff meetings and serve on committees through actual discussion and contribution

tasks.design: Link the existing agenda and papers from {CALENDAR} to {DOCS}. Keep the assistant's reading and meeting contribution human; no extra minutes or report is created.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meeting papers may require repeated retrieval from separate locations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing agenda links can remove that navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding issues, contributing experience and working with colleagues require participation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant contributes firsthand classroom knowledge and responds to colleagues.

ambition.what: Meeting and committee participation remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: agenda links can reduce paper retrieval while reading and committee participation remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is actual meeting preparation and participation. This assistant is not assumed to be the minute-taker or report author; no trailing record is invented.

The existing meeting organizer supplies dated agenda, meeting ID and actual paper links. s1 counts reading, checking and manual missing-paper lookup; no new structured agenda capture is assumed. Try native agenda links first; remove3 of15 retrieval units, retaining12 for reading. All85 participation units remain.
No automated decision, recording or external send is proposed. Estimates are unmeasured; incremental link repair beyond normal paper reading is counted below.
research_questions: Observe what the assistant actually reads and whether any record-writing duty really exists.

already_counted.description: Paper reading and all participation remain in s1-s2.

incremental.description: Maintain paper references and repair broken links beyond normal meeting preparation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=12+85=97. Gross3 less0.5 upkeep gives2.5. Conservative case: late committee papers retain14.5 of15 preparation units; the0.5 gain only covers upkeep.

steps.what: Locate the actual presentation files and equipment operating references
Set up and test the computers, audio-visual aids and actual presentation materials
Use the presentation equipment and materials in time with the teacher's actual presentation

tasks.design: Use the existing presentation-file links in {DOCS} and the classroom equipment's {OTHER} native shortcuts. Retain equipment setup, actual tests and live operation; the change removes repeated file hunting only.
tasks.previous_blocker: The correct teacher-selected files and equipment references can be scattered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native file shortcuts can locate the actual presentation without changing its content.
tasks.still_hard: Connections, sound, visibility, timing and faults require physical checking and live operation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices what the audience and teacher need and responds during the presentation.

ambition.what: The same presentation support remains human.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native file shortcuts can reduce presentation-file retrieval while physical setup and live equipment operation remain human.

assumptions: {OTHER} means actual classroom computers, displays and audio equipment. Boundary is retrieving existing teacher-selected files, setup/testing and live use, not creating a new presentation or public broadcast.

The responsible teacher already supplies file/version and lesson reference; the existing equipment owner supplies operating instructions. s1 retains checking the correct version and manual missing-file lookup. s2 counts all compatibility tests and repair; s3 all timing and operation. No clean new media package is assumed.

Test native shortcuts first. s1 removes6 of15 repeated file-navigation units and retains9 for version/source checking. No cut touches setup or operation; existing media runtime earns no saving. Estimates are unmeasured and specific to actual manual file hunting.
No new report, pupil data capture or external release is invented. Additional broken-shortcut maintenance beyond retained setup faults is counted below.
research_questions: Observe correct-file retrieval separately from equipment setup and live operation.
Test a changed file format and a broken shortcut with physical setup repair retained.

already_counted.description: Correct-file checking, all physical setup/testing and live operation remain in s1-s3.

incremental.description: Maintain file shortcuts and equipment-reference links beyond retained setup fault repair.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=9+25+60=94. Gross6 less1 upkeep gives5. Conservative case: a new presentation format and unlinked version require14 of15 retrieval units; the1-unit gain only covers upkeep, with all setup and operation retained.

steps.what: Read the teacher's actual lesson-material brief and display or demonstration requirements
Draft the actual lesson handouts, display wording and demonstration labels required by the teacher

loop.purpose: Draft wording and label layout within the teacher's supplied content and brief.
loop.input: Actual brief, provided sources and current assistant preparation notes.
loop.output: Draft handout text, display captions and labels with source references.
loop.check: Assistant checks every factual statement and instruction against the source, age/access requirements and brief; teacher makes final educational review after preparation.
loop.stop: Unsupported content or unsuitable instructions stop for manual rewrite, after at most two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied explanatory text needs composition; reuse supplied text and fixed labels without a model where possible.

steps.what: Prepare the actual physical lesson materials, exhibits, equipment and demonstration components
outputs: final prepared physical materials and display layout

steps.what: Review the final prepared lesson materials, display layout and demonstration setup under the teacher's actual instructional responsibility
inputs: final prepared physical materials and display layout

steps.what: Place the exact teacher-checked lesson materials, displays and equipment in their intended classroom positions

tasks.design: Reuse the current {DOCS} material template and draft only varied text from the teacher's actual brief. The assistant retains all physical preparation with classroom supplies {OTHER}; the responsible teacher checks the final prepared version before the actual classroom placement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material captions and handouts require repeated first-draft wording alongside substantial physical preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded text draft can reduce that wording work without replacing cutting, printing, equipment preparation or teacher review.
tasks.still_hard: Age suitability, accessibility and the actual physical exhibit or demonstration require direct checking.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant makes the material usable and the teacher retains instructional responsibility.

ambition.what: Prepare the same teacher-directed classroom materials with less first-draft text work.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a source-bound draft can support handout and display wording, while physical preparation and the responsible teacher's final material review remain human.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual material/display preparation through intended classroom placement. The teacher's existing brief supplies topic, source content, goal and access constraints. s1 counts reading and clarification; s2 retains actual note capture, corrections and source checks, s3 all physical preparation, and s5 all placement. No free new structured lesson brief is assumed.

{OTHER} means classroom printing, craft and demonstration equipment. Test existing templates and teacher-provided material reuse first. s2 removes15 of30 first-draft organization units and retains15 for capture, meaning checks and rewrite. All other focal work remains unchanged; estimates are unmeasured.

s4 is the class teacher's actual final instructional review, not an added manager or the assistant approving her own notes. Confirm that real route; do not invent a new approval hierarchy. The exact finished materials and layout exist before s4; altered content, physical layout or placement voids a1.

Ordinary working file saves within s2 are near-zero, fully retained and ungated without benefit. Additional source packaging and failed-draft repair are counted below; existing teacher review is not deducted again or transferred unpaid. No pupil recording, scoring or public external publication is proposed.
unknowns: Actual wording versus physical preparation effort
Existing material templates and final teacher review route
research_questions: Trace the real brief, text draft, physical preparation and final teacher review.
Test a changed physical layout after review and an unsupported caption; require correction and fresh authorization before placement.

already_counted.description: Brief reading, actual note capture/correction, all physical preparation and final placement remain in s1, s2, s3 and s5.
The actual teacher's final material review remains other-role work, excluded from the assistant denominator.

incremental.description: Additional source packaging, template upkeep and failed-draft repairs beyond retained assistant corrections.

approvals.approved_version: Exact final physical materials, display content/layout and intended placement reviewed in s4; any change voids authorization.

Conservative case: unfamiliar subject and highly individual display wording retain27 of30 draft units, leaving3/95*100 less3=0.1578, low rounded down to0.1. Physical preparation, placement and teacher review are unchanged.
